postTitle: Gig and Informal Work: Planning Without an Employer
topic: Uneven freelance income can become a steady monthly salary

assumptions.notes: One freelance year, monthly income: Jan €1,800, Feb €4,200, Mar €900, Apr €3,600, May €2,700, Jun €5,100, Jul €1,200, Aug €3,300, Sep €2,400, Oct €4,500, Nov €600, Dec €3,900. Total €34,200. 25% set aside for tax (illustrative): €8,550. Left after tax €25,650, about €2,140 a month (25,650 ÷ 12 = 2,137.5). Fixed salary €2,000 a month, €24,000 a year. Holding account running balance lowest at €825 below zero in March; year ends €1,650 ahead (25,650 minus 24,000). Illustrative.

card.title: THE SALARY METHOD
card.footnote: Illustrative. The tax share depends on local rules.

hookVariants.narration: Part two: even at the right rate, pay swings from six hundred to five thousand one hundred a month. What do you pay yourself?

beats.narration: Every payment lands in one holding account, and here a quarter goes to tax first.
A fixed salary comes out, from a month's buffer, so thin months draw it down and big months refill it.
That's two thousand a month, just under the after tax average.
The salary method: one account, tax first, a fixed salary.

caption.instagram:
Your income swings from €600 to €5,100. Your rent doesn't. So what do you pay yourself?

Every payment lands in one holding account and 25% goes to tax first. A fixed €2,000 salary comes out each month, just under the after tax average. Thin months draw the account down, big months refill it. With one month's buffer to start, it never ran dry.
